blocks.body: The base case is the branch that returns a value without calling itself again.

Every time a function calls itself, Python sets aside a new frame to hold that call's own variables.

The frames pile onto the call stack, one per call still waiting to finish, and nothing is cleared away until something returns.

The recursive case is the other branch, the one that adds another frame.

A function needs both: the recursive case makes progress toward the base case, and the base case stops it.

blocks.body: Without a base case the stack depth just grows. Python stops you at its recursion limit and raises RecursionError, so the failure is a crash rather than a hang.

blocks.mentalModel: The recursive case gets you closer; the base case is the only thing that stops.
progression: read the function and find the branch with no self-call
